description: Toshiba GR200 GRL200 distance elements of setting group 1 (Prot/G1/Trip/Distance_ZS for the phase-fault elements, Distance_ZG for the earth-fault elements). Catalog-only, verified subset: the phase / earth element enables, the agreed element direction, the phase mho reach and angle, the earth quadrilateral resistive reach, the phase / earth timers, the characteristic selections and the fault-locator line data. The phase elements are MHO with blinders and the earth elements QUAD on the sample: one canonical characteristic per zone cannot represent both, so the characteristic is recorded as not representable and the blinder / boundary geometry is preserved with each zone. No CT / VT setting and no impedance basis are stated on the sheet (the CT ratio appears only in the notes).
interpretation_notes: The zones are the sheet's Zn phase-fault elements (ZnS, Distance_ZS) and earth-fault elements (ZnG, Distance_ZG) of setting group 1 (the sheet's Active Group is 1): Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, Z5 and the extension zone Z1X. The command zones (ZCS / ZCG) are not mapped.

Each zone's phase and earth elements are enabled separately (mapped as Phase-Phase Faults / Earth Faults). The sheet states no single zone in-service switch, so the zone's status is not derived from them (Missing).
The zone's direction is mapped only when its phase and earth elements state the same direction.

Phase elements: ZS-Chara (MHO on this sheet) with resistive / directional blinders; earth elements: ZG-Chara (QUAD). One canonical characteristic cannot represent a MHO phase element and a QUAD earth element at once, so the characteristic is recorded as not representable (never forced into one). The mho reach and angle are kept as the zone's Reach; the blinders, the earth reactance reach and the earth mho settings are preserved with the zone.
Krs / Kxs (and Krm / Kxm) are per-zone percent compensation factors in the relay's own definition, not the canonical Kr / Kx; they are preserved with the zone, not converted.
No CT / VT setting is on the sheet (the CT ratio in the notes is not a setting) and the impedance basis is not stated: none is assumed.

zone_preserved.reason: Mho / quadrilateral boundary and blinder geometry of the zone's elements (reactance and resistive blinders, blinder and reactance-line angles, earth compensation factors). The combined phase-mho / earth-quad shape with blinders is a capability gap of the current model: preserved, not drawn and not approximated.
Output, blocking and switch-on-to-fault logic of the zone's element; not part of the zone geometry and not interpreted.

mappings.note: The fault locator's line 1 R1 / X1 read as the line's positive-sequence impedance (the sheet's own '1' / '0' naming, not a stated label).
The fault locator's line 1 R0 / X0 read as the line's zero-sequence impedance (the sheet's own '1' / '0' naming, not a stated label).
The direction both of the zone's elements state (ZnS-Dir, ZnG-Dir). Elements that disagree leave the zone's direction unresolved.

ZS-Chara (phase-fault elements) and ZG-Chara (earth-fault elements). When they differ, one zone characteristic cannot represent both: the characteristic is recorded as not representable (unknown), never as one of the two.
The phase-fault element's mho reach (ZnS-Mho.Reach) at its characteristic angle (ZnS-Mho.Angle). Its blinders are preserved with the zone.
The earth-fault element's resistive reach (ZnG-R.Reach), as printed. Its boundary is inclined at ZnG-R.Angle (preserved); the phase-phase engine does not draw it.
